target_customer: Coaches, trainers, creators and knowledge businesses, mainly in India, who pay for software to sell courses, webinars and consultations
problem: Independent coaches and creators stitch together separate tools for payments, scheduling, courses, CRM and marketing.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payment-linked fees for creators

founders.name: Suyash Sinha
education: IIM Calcutta (graduated 2015 per IIM Calcutta page)
founders.background_notes: Batchmate of Rawat at IIM Calcutta.

founders.name: Akhil Tripathi
founders.background_notes: Named among founders by Inc42 in 2024; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: At founding it was a consumer event marketplace app with host verification; later a standard SaaS stack with payments and website builder.

defensibility.rationale: Creators store customers, payments and branded apps in the platform, which gives some switching cost, but similar tools were plentiful.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not applicable after the pivot; no incumbent acquired the company.

market_need_then: In 2017 the founders found strong demand for hosting and attending home social events (about 500 sign-ups a day from a Google form and Facebook page); the creator-tool need appeared after the pivot.

identity.voice_and_tone: Creator and profit focused tagline: Super App that maximizes profits

rebrands.why: The social experience business was hard to run in the pandemic; the company pivoted to creator tools (per a profile; not the company)

branding.community_and_virality: Company claims 100,000+ creators; no source shows brand-driven virality.

brand_strength.rationale: A new invented name after the pivot with modest press, and the secondary domain exlyapp.com suggests little brand pull.

pivots.from: MyScoot, a marketplace for home-hosted social events
pivots.to: Exly, a business platform for coaches and creators
pivots.why: Pandemic made the event business hard to run, per a press profile

outcome_analysis: The company started as MyScoot, a social events marketplace that raised $1.7M in 2019, then pivoted to a creator and coach SaaS platform called Exly. It grew to a reported 95 person team and raised $6.2M led by Chiratae in March 2024, so the pivot appears to have found a market, though revenue is not disclosed.
notes: YourStory 2019 article was blocked (403); the $1.7M July 2019 seed with Lightspeed, Venture Highway and Mayfield comes from a search result summary of that article, while Inc42 says the earlier seed was $1.8M with no date; amount conflict. CB Insights labels the 2024 round Series A but no press does, so stage is other. The company was MyScoot at the batch, so Exly competitors named by Inc42 (Yellowdig, KickUp, AEFIS, Acrobatiq, Quipper) are post-pivot edtech names and not used. No dated rival found for the 2019 social events model. Founding year 2017 (incorporated December 2017 per IIM Calcutta page); Inc42 says 2018 then 2021.
